about: What release 1 of the Mushroom Character Vocabulary holds and how its identifiers are made. build_release.py reads this file.
decided: Will, 2026-11-22 11:24, on the report that step 1 waited for his word: "go". The whole list in one release and the handover all at once are Claude's picks of the same hour, told to him before the build. Will, 2026-11-22 18:35, shown three characters beside the sentences of the first list quoted for them, and told that the license of those sentences was open: "The character is pileus striate and the options are Yes or No. All of these can be Yes or No. No need to include so much text. Regarding permissions, XDE said "You've got my blessing to do as you wish and how you best see things to be presented." which settles the issue." So: the sentences of the first list are not quoted in a release, each character names the item it came from, and the permission is settled by him.

identifiers.form: MCV_ and seven digits. The number means nothing: it is only the order in which an identifier was given.
rules: An identifier is given once and never reused. It is never deleted: a retired one stays in the register with a pointer to what replaced it.

An identifier names a part, a character or a value option of one character. A value option used by several characters has one identifier for each of them, so that each character can carry its own description of it (Will, 2026-11-19 10:51, on the description of such a value option: "Each character gets its own").
The wording may change from release to release; the identifier does not. The words as written stay on record beside the words shown.

The register, identifiers.csv, is add-only. It is kept beside the folder of the release, with build_release.py and release_rules.json. build_release.py keeps every identifier it finds there and gives the next number to anything new.

A thing that has no key in the MRDBID database is keyed in the register in another way: a new character by the label the rebuilt list gave it (NEW-1, NEW-2), an added value option by the key of its character and the letters of its name as first given. If such a name is changed in a later release, the rules of that release carry the identifier over; it is not given a new one.

restarted_before_publication.why: Nothing was published. Will's word of 2026-11-22 18:35 replaced six value options of three characters by the general list and gave a fourth character that list. The candidate's register, which no site or person had used, was given afresh once, so that release 1 carries no number that names nothing. build_release.py starts afresh only if it finds exactly that candidate's register.

license_note: The open list is Will Johnston's own compilation. Most of its characters were parsed from the first list, used by its author's permission of 2026-11-13. His words: "You've got my blessing to do as you wish and how you best see things to be presented." He named no license; that his permission covers a CC0 release is Will Johnston's decision of 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-22. The sentences of the first list are not carried in this release. Where words of that list are the reason for a change, or for a topic left to users, they are quoted there, a short sentence or a phrase at a time. Words taken from a source that has a license of its own on record keep that license and are kept in a folder of their own. Where no reuse license is on record for a source, a description taken from it is not reissued and the source is named instead; the names of value options are listed, each with its source.
mission: Will Johnston, 2026-11-14: "The goal is to improve the accuracy of fungi data by providing tools to citizen scientists and others that make this goal easier."
consumption_line: No advice about consumption. MRDBID records how sources describe fungi. It is not a guide to eating, using or handling any fungus, and nothing here says whether any fungus is safe. Values about chemistry or toxicity are reported only as their source states them.
status_line: A proposal for use. Nobody can declare a standard; adoption comes from use. Every part, character and value option is marked proposed.

public_text: A release carries no path of the workspace it was made in and no note that only the workspace can read: no code of the review sheet, no clock time without its date, no row number or file of the working folders. A basis may name the compiler's decision by its date. public_bases holds the rewordings, each a pattern and what replaces it; build_release.py stops if one of them finds nothing, and it stops if such a note is still in a file of the release.
